message: I've filed a patent application for INTERACTIVE ELECTRONIC GREETING CARDS WITH TAP AND TOUCH ACTIVATED EFFECTS.

The invention is an interactive greeting card featuring an internal electronics module that plays multiple digital audio files. It utilizes a slide switch to initiate playback upon opening the card and a touch-sensitive mechanism that triggers additional audio content based on specific physical interactions, such as tapping or a continuous back-and-forth motion.

lines: An interactive greeting card comprising:
a greeting card body having a plurality of greeting card panels, two of the greeting card panels forming an enclosed cavity;

an electronics module contained within the enclosed cavity of the greeting card body, the electronics module comprising a circuit board, an integrated circuit, a touch sensor switch, a speaker, a memory storage device, a power source, a switch, a touch sensor switch plate, and at least two digital audio files saved on the memory storage device;
a first switch which initiates playback of a first digital audio file upon opening the greeting card;
a second switch which initiates playback of a second digital audio file upon human contact with an area of the greeting proximate to the touch sensor switch plate.
An interactive greeting card comprising:

a greeting card body having a first panel connected to a second panel along a first fold line, and a third panel connected to the second panel along a second fold line, the second and third panels attached to form an enclosed cavity therebetween;

an electronics module contained within the enclosed cavity, the electronics module comprising a printed circuit board, a integrated circuit, a controller, a speaker, a memory storage device, two or more digital audio files contained saved on the memory storage device, a power source, a touch sensitive switch including a touch sensor switch plate, and a slide switch;
wherein the slide switch initiates playback of one of the two or more digital audio files, and

wherein the touch sensitive switch initiates playback of one of the two or more digital audio files when a human applies a continuous back and forth motion to an area of the greeting card proximate to the touch sensor switch plate.
An interactive greeting card comprising:
a greeting card body having at least three panels;
an electronics module contained within a cavity formed between two of the at least three panels of the greeting card body, the electronics module comprising:
a printed circuit board;
an integrated circuit;
a touch sensor switch;
a touch sensor switch plate;
a slide switch;
a speaker;
a power source;
a memory storage device, the memory storage device having at least two digital audio files saved thereon;
wherein the slide switch controls playback of a first digital audio file and the touch sensor switch controls playback of a second digital audio file.

message: The application is complete and has been accepted for examination.
The application has been published.

The invention is an interactive greeting card featuring an internal electronics module that utilizes multiple digital audio files stored on a memory device. These files are triggered by a combination of switches, including touch-sensitive sensors and slide mechanisms, to provide specific audio content or verbal instructions to the user. The card design incorporates printed indicia and specific physical interactions, such as back-and-forth motions or unfolding panels, to create an immersive, responsive multimedia experience.

message: I have submitted amendments to claims 1, 8, 15, and 17–19 to address concerns regarding indefiniteness and to clarify that our interactive greeting card requires continuous user motion for audio playback. I respectfully request the withdrawal of the rejections and the issuance of a Notice of Allowance, as the cited prior art does not teach or suggest these specific interactive features.

This Office action is made final, as your recent amendments have necessitated new grounds of rejection. The application remains rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 112 for lack of antecedent basis and under 35 U.S.C. § 103 for obviousness, and the drawings are objected to for failing to show all claimed features.
I've filed a response to the final rejection.

The invention is an interactive greeting card featuring an internal electronics module that plays back multiple digital audio files based on specific user interactions. The current claims define a device where audio playback is strictly tied to continuous user input—such as persistent pressure, specific rubbing motions, or back-and-forth movements—ensuring that audio ceases immediately when the interaction stops. Furthermore, the invention incorporates features that allow the speed of the user's motion to dynamically control the playback volume or tempo of the audio files.

message: I have submitted amendments to address the indefiniteness rejections by clarifying claim language and providing proper antecedent basis. Additionally, I contend that the 35 U.S.C. § 103 rejections are improper because the cited prior art is not analogous and fails to teach the novel, user-interactive audio controls unique to my greeting card invention. Accordingly, I respectfully request the withdrawal of all rejections and the allowance of the pending claims.
I've filed a Request for Continued Examination.
I've submitted claim amendments with the Request for Continued Examination.

The invention is an interactive greeting card featuring an internal electronics module that enables audio playback through specific user interactions, such as continuous back-and-forth rubbing motions on designated card areas. Recent amendments refine these interactions by specifying that the speed and volume of the audio playback are dynamically controlled by the velocity of the user’s physical input. This design ensures that audio is tied directly to user activity, pausing immediately when the motion stops and resuming from that point if the interaction is re-initiated.
